The latest general 2026 call states: «En caso de certificados de título y/o grado académico, obtenidos en el extranjero, deberá ser acreditado de conformidad a la ley. Debidamente apostillados o legalizados» and «Adjuntar traducción al español». It also requires «Fotocopia Cédula de Identidad o permiso de residencia vigente»; it does not state Chilean nationality. international.notes: The published Medicina curriculum includes Spanish-titled medical subjects and four English-language courses (“Inglés Comunicacional I–IV”); UBB does not identify any Medicine subject as taught in English. The international office is the Dirección General de Relaciones Institucionales, which administers international mobility.

profile_paragraphs: UBB’s Medicine degree belongs to the Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud y de los Alimentos (FACSA). It is delivered at Campus Fernando May in Chillán, lasts 14 semesters, and awards the Médico/a Cirujano/a title and Licenciatura en Medicina.
FACSA was created in 1989 under another name and received its present name in 1993. Its current dean is Dr María Pía Gianelli Barra; the School of Medicine is directed by Dr Elías Kassisse El Hage.

Medicine is a new programme: in May 2025 UBB began its self-evaluation process for the degree’s first accreditation. This indicates a young faculty programme rather than an established postgraduate medical-specialty centre.

Clinical teaching is developing in Ñuble. In September 2026 third-year students began practical Semiología 2 activities at Hospital de San Carlos, continuing activity already begun at Hospital Clínico Herminda Martín.

For a foreign clinician, a teaching approach is more realistic than immediate independent clinical practice: UBB’s published Medicine recruitment precedent required a foreign MD to be validated in Chile and a foreign specialty to have Chilean certification.

unknowns: No official UBB or teaching-hospital page located that names a rheumatology unit, department, or service. A public procurement record shows adult-rheumatology consultations at Hospital Clínico Herminda Martín, but says institutional staffing could not cover them; this is insufficient to invent a formal unit.
No rheumatology specialty/beca programme was found. FACSA’s official postgraduate menu lists four non-rheumatology programmes.
UBB publishes no English-medium Medicine course. The conclusion is based on the official published curriculum; it should not be interpreted as proof that individual staff never use English.
No academic vacancies were open on the official concursos page on 3 September 2026; consequently there is no current Medicine/Internal Medicine vacancy or current vacancy-specific HR contact.
